topics.title: Polar Science 101
topics.description: The essentials of ice, oceans, climate and polar fieldwork.

questions.question: Which Indian station is located in the Arctic?
questions.explanation: Himadri is India's Arctic research station, located in Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard. Maitri and Bharati are both in Antarctica.

questions.question: What does glaciology study?
questions.explanation: Glaciology is the scientific study of glaciers, ice sheets, and ice in general — how they form, move, and respond to climate changes.

questions.question: Why are polar regions important to climate science?
options: They store signals of Earth's climate
They are closest to the Sun
questions.explanation: Polar ice cores, sediments, and ocean records preserve signals of Earth's past and present climate, making polar regions critical natural archives.

topics.title: Antarctica vs Arctic
topics.description: Two poles, two systems, one connected planet.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the Arctic and Antarctica?
options: Antarctica is a continent, the Arctic is an ocean
questions.explanation: Antarctica is a land continent covered by ice, while the Arctic is primarily an ocean surrounded by land.

questions.question: Which polar region has penguins?
questions.explanation: Penguins are found only in the Southern Hemisphere, primarily in and around Antarctica.

questions.question: What connects Arctic and Antarctic climate systems?
questions.explanation: Global ocean circulation, including deep thermohaline circulation, connects the polar regions and influences climate patterns worldwide.

topics.title: Climate change
topics.description: Read the signals recorded in ice, air and ocean.

questions.question: What can ice cores tell us about past climate?
options: Temperature and atmospheric composition over millennia
questions.explanation: Ice cores trap air bubbles from past atmospheres, allowing scientists to reconstruct temperature and CO₂ levels going back hundreds of thousands of years.

questions.question: Why is polar ice melting a global concern?
options: It contributes to sea level rise
It creates more freshwater for drinking
questions.explanation: Melting polar ice contributes directly to global sea level rise, threatening coastal communities, and alters ocean circulation patterns.

questions.question: What is the albedo effect in polar regions?
options: Ice and snow reflecting sunlight back to space
questions.explanation: The albedo effect refers to ice and snow reflecting solar radiation. As ice melts, darker surfaces absorb more heat, creating a feedback loop.

topics.title: Glaciology
topics.description: How glaciers move, melt and remember climate.

questions.question: How do glaciers move?
questions.explanation: Glaciers move through internal deformation (ice crystals deforming under pressure) and basal sliding (the glacier sliding over bedrock).

questions.question: What is a calving event?
options: Ice breaking off a glacier into the ocean
questions.explanation: Calving is the process where chunks of ice break off the terminus of a glacier or ice shelf and fall into the ocean, forming icebergs.

questions.question: What does the mass balance of a glacier measure?
options: The difference between snow accumulation and ice loss
questions.explanation: Mass balance compares how much snow/ice a glacier gains versus loses. A negative balance means the glacier is shrinking.

topics.title: Polar oceans
topics.description: Currents, carbon and the ocean around the ice.

questions.question: Why is the Southern Ocean important for global climate?
options: It absorbs significant CO₂ and drives deep ocean circulation
questions.explanation: The Southern Ocean absorbs a disproportionate amount of atmospheric CO₂ and heat, and its dense cold waters drive global thermohaline circulation.

questions.question: What is thermohaline circulation?
options: Global ocean circulation driven by temperature and salinity differences
questions.explanation: Thermohaline circulation is a global system of deep ocean currents driven by differences in water density due to temperature and salinity.

questions.question: What lives beneath Antarctic sea ice?
options: A rich ecosystem including krill, algae, and fish
questions.explanation: The underside of Antarctic sea ice supports a rich ecosystem: algae grows on the ice, feeding krill, which supports fish, seals, and whales.

questions.question: When was India's first Antarctic station, Dakshin Gangotri, established?
questions.explanation: Dakshin Gangotri was established in 1983 during India's first Antarctic expedition. It was later buried by ice and replaced by Maitri in 1989.

questions.question: What type of research does Bharati station primarily support?
options: Ocean, climate, life and earth sciences
questions.explanation: Bharati, established in 2012, is designed for multi-disciplinary research across ocean, climate, life, and earth sciences.

questions.question: Where is India's Arctic station Himadri located?
questions.explanation: Himadri is located in Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard (Norway), one of the northernmost research settlements in the world at 79°N.
